meta.title: 03.Advanced English Proficiency Test (C1-C2)
meta.description: A comprehensive 30-question advanced English grammar and syntax test featuring multi-error detection, tailored for Indonesian participants.

questions.question: The sentence may contain 0, 1, or multiple errors. Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form. If no error, choose No Error.
questions.explanation: Negative adverbials at the beginning of a sentence require subject-auxiliary inversion.

description.en: When a negative adverbial is placed at the beginning of a sentence for emphasis, the subject and auxiliary verb must be inverted.
description.id: Ketika adverbial negatif diletakkan di awal kalimat untuk penekanan, subjek dan kata kerja bantu harus dibalik.

wrong_correct.wrong: Rarely we have seen such talent.
wrong_correct.correct: Rarely have we seen such talent.

explanation.en: Inversion is required after 'Rarely'.

en.introduction: Inversion adds formal emphasis. The auxiliary verb comes before the subject.

rules.title: 1. Basic Structure
rules.explanation: Negative adverb + auxiliary + subject + main verb.
rules.structure: Rarely + have/has/did + subject + V3/V1
notes: Applies to: rarely, seldom, never, hardly, scarcely, no sooner

common_mistakes.wrong: Never I will forget this.
common_mistakes.correct: Never will I forget this.

other_examples.sentence: Seldom has the company faced such a crisis.
other_examples.translation: Jarang sekali perusahaan menghadapi krisis seperti ini.

explanation.en: Emphasizes the rarity of the crisis.

questions.question: The sentence may contain 0, 1, or multiple errors. Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form. If no error, choose No Error.
questions.explanation: This is a correct mixed conditional sentence: past condition (had taken) with a present result (would be living).

description.en: Mixed conditionals combine different time frames, typically a past condition with a present result.
description.id: Conditional campuran menggabungkan kerangka waktu yang berbeda, biasanya kondisi masa lalu dengan hasil masa kini.

en.introduction: Mixed conditionals allow us to express complex hypothetical situations across different time periods.

rules.title: 1. Past Condition, Present Result
rules.explanation: If-clause uses past perfect, main clause uses would + base verb.
rules.structure: If + subject + had + V3, subject + would + V1
notes: Used for past actions affecting the present.

common_mistakes.wrong: If he had taken the job, he would have been living in Paris now.
common_mistakes.correct: If he had taken the job, he would be living in Paris now.
common_mistakes.reason: 'Now' requires a present result (would be), not a past result (would have been).

other_examples.sentence: If I had studied medicine, I would be a doctor now.
other_examples.translation: Jika saya belajar kedokteran, saya akan menjadi dokter sekarang.

explanation.en: Past study affects present profession.
explanation.id: Kuliah masa lalu memengaruhi profesi saat ini.

questions.question: The sentence may contain 0, 1, or multiple errors. Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form. If no error, choose No Error.
questions.explanation: The active participle 'Having finished' should be used because the project manager finished the report. 'Having been finished' is passive and incorrect here.

description.en: Perfect participle clauses show that one action was completed before another began. The voice must match the subject.
description.id: Klausa partisip sempurna menunjukkan bahwa satu tindakan selesai sebelum yang lain dimulai. Suara (aktif/pasif) harus sesuai dengan subjek.

wrong_correct.wrong: Having been finished the report, she left.
wrong_correct.correct: Having finished the report, she left.

explanation.en: Active subject requires active participle.

en.introduction: Participle clauses make writing more concise and formal.

rules.title: 1. Active Perfect Participle
rules.explanation: Used when the subject performed the action.
rules.structure: Having + V3 + object, subject + main verb
notes: Subject of participle must be the same as main clause subject.

common_mistakes.wrong: Having been read the book, I returned it.
common_mistakes.correct: Having read the book, I returned it.
common_mistakes.reason: The subject 'I' actively read the book.

other_examples.sentence: Having completed the course, she received her certificate.
other_examples.translation: Setelah menyelesaikan kursus, dia menerima sertifikatnya.

explanation.en: Completion precedes receiving.

questions.question: The sentence may contain 0, 1, or multiple errors. Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form. If no error, choose No Error.
questions.explanation: The subjunctive mood correctly uses the base form 'be evaluated' after 'It is essential that'.

description.en: The mandative subjunctive uses the base form of the verb after expressions of necessity, importance, or suggestion.
description.id: Subjunktif mandatif menggunakan bentuk dasar kata kerja setelah ekspresi kebutuhan, kepentingan, atau saran.

en.introduction: The subjunctive is formal and common in academic or legal English.

rules.title: 1. Mandative Subjunctive
rules.explanation: Base form of the verb is used regardless of the subject.
rules.structure: It is essential/important/vital that + subject + base verb
notes: Common triggers: essential, crucial, imperative, suggest, recommend

common_mistakes.wrong: It is essential that he is evaluated.
common_mistakes.correct: It is essential that he be evaluated.

other_examples.sentence: The committee recommended that the proposal be reviewed.
other_examples.translation: Komite merekomendasikan agar proposal tersebut ditinjau.

explanation.en: Base form 'be' used after 'recommended that'.

questions.question: The sentence may contain 0, 1, or multiple errors. Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form. If no error, choose No Error.
questions.explanation: Parallel structure requires all items in the list to follow the same grammatical form. Since it starts with 'reducing', the others must be 'improving' and 'enhancing'.

description.en: Parallel structure requires that items in a list or series share the same grammatical form.
description.id: Struktur paralel mengharuskan item dalam daftar atau seri memiliki bentuk tata bahasa yang sama.

wrong_correct.wrong: The policy aims at reducing costs, to improve efficiency, and enhancing productivity.
wrong_correct.correct: The policy aims at reducing costs, improving efficiency, and enhancing productivity.

explanation.en: All items must be gerunds to match 'reducing'.
explanation.id: Semua item harus berupa gerund agar sesuai dengan 'reducing'.

en.introduction: Parallelism ensures clarity and rhythm in writing.

rules.title: 1. Lists and Series
rules.explanation: Items joined by conjunctions must match in form.
rules.structure: verb-ing, verb-ing, and verb-ing
notes: Applies to nouns, infinitives, gerunds, and clauses.

common_mistakes.wrong: She likes hiking, swimming, and to ride bikes.
common_mistakes.correct: She likes hiking, swimming, and riding bikes.

other_examples.sentence: The software is designed to be fast, reliable, and secure.
other_examples.translation: Perangkat lunak ini dirancang agar cepat, andal, dan aman.

explanation.en: All adjectives in the series.

questions.question: The sentence may contain 0, 1, or multiple errors. Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form. If no error, choose No Error.
questions.explanation: In 'It-cleft' sentences, 'that' is preferred over 'which' to introduce the relative clause, especially when emphasizing a non-human subject in formal English.

description.en: Cleft sentences are used to emphasize a specific part of a sentence by splitting it into two clauses.
description.id: Kalimat cleft digunakan untuk menekankan bagian tertentu dari kalimat dengan membaginya menjadi dua klausa.

wrong_correct.wrong: It was the strategy which led to success.
wrong_correct.correct: It was the strategy that led to success.

explanation.en: 'That' is the standard relative pronoun in it-clefts.
explanation.id: 'That' adalah kata ganti relatif standar dalam it-clefts.

en.introduction: Clefts shift the focus to the emphasized element.

rules.title: 1. It-Cleft Structure
rules.explanation: Starts with 'It + be + emphasized element + that/who clause'.
rules.structure: It + is/was + focus + that + clause
notes: Use 'who' for people, 'that' for things or people.

common_mistakes.wrong: It was John which called me.
common_mistakes.correct: It was John who called me.

other_examples.sentence: It was the heavy rain that caused the flood.
other_examples.translation: Hujan deras itulah yang menyebabkan banjir.

explanation.en: Emphasizes 'the heavy rain' as the cause.

questions.question: The sentence may contain 0, 1, or multiple errors. Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form. If no error, choose No Error.
questions.explanation: The sentence is correct. 'By which' is the appropriate formal relative pronoun phrase indicating the method or means.

description.en: In formal English, prepositions are placed before the relative pronoun (which/whom).
description.id: Dalam bahasa Inggris formal, preposisi diletakkan sebelum kata ganti relatif (which/whom).

en.introduction: This structure is highly formal and common in academic writing.

rules.title: 1. Preposition + Which/Whom
rules.explanation: The preposition relates to the verb or noun in the relative clause.
rules.structure: noun + preposition + which/whom + clause
notes: Do not use 'that' after a preposition.

common_mistakes.wrong: The method that we relied on was flawed.
common_mistakes.correct: The method on which we relied was flawed.

other_examples.sentence: The criteria according to which candidates are judged are strict.
other_examples.translation: Kriteria yang digunakan untuk menilai kandidat sangat ketat.

explanation.en: 'According to which' refers to the criteria.

questions.question: The sentence may contain 0, 1, or multiple errors. Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form. If no error, choose No Error.
questions.explanation: 'The number of' takes a singular verb ('has'), whereas 'A number of' takes a plural verb ('have').

description.en: 'The number of' refers to a single statistical figure, requiring a singular verb.
description.id: 'The number of' merujuk pada angka statistik tunggal, memerlukan kata kerja tunggal.

wrong_correct.wrong: The number of applicants have risen.
wrong_correct.correct: The number of applicants has risen.

explanation.en: 'The number' is singular.

en.introduction: Agreement depends on the head noun of the subject phrase.

rules.title: 1. The number vs. A number
rules.explanation: 'The number' is singular; 'A number' is plural.
rules.structure: The number of + plural noun + singular verb
notes: A number of + plural noun + plural verb

common_mistakes.wrong: The number of cars are increasing.
common_mistakes.correct: The number of cars is increasing.

other_examples.sentence: A number of issues remain unresolved.
other_examples.translation: Sejumlah masalah masih belum terselesaikan.

explanation.en: 'A number of' acts as a plural quantifier.
explanation.id: 'A number of' bertindak sebagai kuantifier jamak.

questions.question: The sentence may contain 0, 1, or multiple errors. Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form. If no error, choose No Error.
questions.explanation: The correct dependent prepositions are 'composed of' and 'capable of' + gerund.

description.en: Certain adjectives and verbs require specific prepositions that must be memorized.
description.id: Kata sifat dan kata kerja tertentu memerlukan preposisi spesifik yang harus dihafal.

wrong_correct.wrong: The team is composed from members capable to work hard.
wrong_correct.correct: The team is composed of members capable of working hard.

explanation.en: 'Composed of' and 'capable of + V-ing' are fixed collocations.
explanation.id: 'Composed of' dan 'capable of + V-ing' adalah kolokasi tetap.

en.introduction: Preposition choice is often idiomatic and does not translate directly.

rules.title: 1. Fixed Prepositions
rules.explanation: Adjectives and past participles often take specific prepositions.
rules.structure: composed of, capable of, interested in
notes: 'Capable' is always followed by 'of + gerund'.

common_mistakes.wrong: She is capable to do it.
common_mistakes.correct: She is capable of doing it.

other_examples.sentence: The cake is made of flour and sugar.
other_examples.translation: Kue itu terbuat dari tepung dan gula.

explanation.en: 'Made of' indicates material.

questions.question: The sentence may contain 0, 1, or multiple errors. Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form. If no error, choose No Error.
questions.explanation: Mid-position adverbs like 'completely' should be placed between the auxiliary verb and the main verb.

description.en: Mid-position adverbs typically appear after the first auxiliary verb or before the main verb.
description.id: Kata keterangan posisi tengah biasanya muncul setelah kata kerja bantu pertama atau sebelum kata kerja utama.

wrong_correct.wrong: The CEO has transformed completely the vision.
wrong_correct.correct: The CEO has completely transformed the vision.

explanation.en: Adverb of degree goes between auxiliary and main verb.
explanation.id: Kata keterangan derajat berada di antara kata kerja bantu dan utama.

en.introduction: Correct adverb placement ensures natural-sounding English.

rules.title: 1. Mid-Position Rule
rules.explanation: Place adverbs of degree after the auxiliary verb.
rules.structure: Subject + auxiliary + adverb + main verb + object
notes: Applies to: completely, totally, almost, never, always

common_mistakes.wrong: I have forgotten totally my keys.
common_mistakes.correct: I have totally forgotten my keys.
common_mistakes.reason: Adverb should not be placed between verb and object.

other_examples.sentence: He has always wanted to visit Japan.
other_examples.translation: Dia selalu ingin mengunjungi Jepang.

explanation.en: 'Always' is correctly placed after 'has'.

questions.question: The sentence may contain 0, 1, or multiple errors. Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form. If no error, choose No Error.
questions.explanation: After modal verbs (should have, must have), the past participle (V3) must be used.

description.en: Past modals express deduction, criticism, or regret about past events using modal + have + V3.
description.id: Modal masa lalu mengekspresikan deduksi, kritik, atau penyesalan tentang peristiwa masa lalu menggunakan modal + have + V3.

wrong_correct.wrong: You should have submit the report.
wrong_correct.correct: You should have submitted the report.

explanation.en: 'Have' must be followed by the past participle (V3).

en.introduction: Past modals are essential for expressing nuanced attitudes toward past actions.

rules.title: 1. Modal + Have + V3
rules.explanation: Used for past deduction, regret, or criticism.
rules.structure: Subject + should/must/could + have + V3
notes: Never use V1 after 'have' in this structure.

common_mistakes.wrong: He must have forgot the meeting.
common_mistakes.correct: He must have forgotten the meeting.

other_examples.sentence: She could have won the race if she hadn't fallen.
other_examples.translation: Dia bisa saja memenangkan lomba jika tidak jatuh.

explanation.en: Expresses a missed past opportunity.
explanation.id: Mengekspresikan peluang masa lalu yang terlewat.

questions.question: The sentence may contain 0, 1, or multiple errors. Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form. If no error, choose No Error.
questions.explanation: The sentence is correct. 'Will have developed' is the correct future perfect tense, indicating an action completed before a specific future time.

description.en: The future perfect tense describes an action that will be completed before a specific point in the future.
description.id: Future perfect menggambarkan tindakan yang akan selesai sebelum titik waktu tertentu di masa depan.

en.introduction: Often used with 'by' or 'by the time'.

rules.title: 1. Future Perfect Structure
rules.explanation: Indicates completion before a future deadline.
rules.structure: Subject + will have + V3 + by + future time
notes: The action is viewed from a future perspective.

common_mistakes.wrong: By tomorrow, I will finish the work.
common_mistakes.correct: By tomorrow, I will have finished the work.
common_mistakes.reason: 'By' requires future perfect to show completion.

other_examples.sentence: They will have arrived by noon.
other_examples.translation: Mereka akan tiba sebelum siang hari.

explanation.en: Completion before noon.

questions.question: The sentence may contain 0, 1, or multiple errors. Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form. If no error, choose No Error.
questions.explanation: To express a present desire for a different state, 'wish' is followed by the past simple, not 'would'.

description.en: 'Wish' + past simple is used to express a desire for a present situation to be different.
description.id: 'Wish' + past simple digunakan untuk mengekspresikan keinginan agar situasi saat ini berbeda.

wrong_correct.wrong: I wish I would know the answer.
wrong_correct.correct: I wish I knew the answer.

explanation.en: Use past simple for present wishes about states.
explanation.id: Gunakan past simple untuk harapan saat ini tentang keadaan.

en.introduction: 'Would' is only used with 'wish' for complaints about others' actions, not for one's own states.

rules.title: 1. Wish + Past Simple
rules.explanation: Used for present states we want to change.
rules.structure: Subject + wish + subject + past simple
notes: Use 'were' instead of 'was' for all subjects in formal English.

common_mistakes.wrong: I wish I have more time.
common_mistakes.correct: I wish I had more time.

other_examples.sentence: If only I lived closer to my family.
other_examples.translation: Andai saja saya tinggal lebih dekat dengan keluarga saya.

explanation.en: Expresses a present regret about location.
explanation.id: Mengekspresikan penyesalan saat ini tentang lokasi.

questions.question: The sentence may contain 0, 1, or multiple errors. Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form. If no error, choose No Error.
questions.explanation: When 'Not only' begins a sentence, it triggers inversion in the first clause.

description.en: 'Not only' at the beginning of a clause requires subject-auxiliary inversion.
description.id: 'Not only' di awal klausa memerlukan inversi subjek-kata kerja bantu.

wrong_correct.wrong: Not only the software is intuitive, but it also offers security.
wrong_correct.correct: Not only is the software intuitive, but it also offers security.

explanation.en: Inversion is mandatory after initial 'Not only'.
explanation.id: Inversi wajib setelah 'Not only' di awal.

en.introduction: This structure adds strong emphasis to the first element.

rules.title: 1. Inversion with Not Only
rules.explanation: Treat 'Not only' like a negative adverbial.
rules.structure: Not only + auxiliary + subject + verb, but + subject + also + verb
notes: Ensure parallel structure in both clauses.

common_mistakes.wrong: Not only she sings, but she also dances.
common_mistakes.correct: Not only does she sing, but she also dances.

other_examples.sentence: Not only did he apologize, but he also offered compensation.
other_examples.translation: Dia tidak hanya meminta maaf, tetapi juga menawarkan kompensasi.

explanation.en: Correct inversion with 'did'.

questions.question: The sentence may contain 0, 1, or multiple errors. Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form. If no error, choose No Error.
questions.explanation: The sentence is correct. 'What the researchers failed to anticipate' functions as a nominal relative clause acting as the subject.

description.en: A nominal relative clause can act as the subject of a sentence.
description.id: Klausa relatif nominal dapat bertindak sebagai subjek kalimat.

en.introduction: This structure is common in academic and formal writing to emphasize the subject.

rules.title: 1. Nominal Relative Subject
rules.explanation: The entire 'what' clause acts as a singular subject.
rules.structure: What + subject + verb + be + complement
notes: The verb 'be' is usually singular.

common_mistakes.wrong: What they need are more time.
common_mistakes.correct: What they need is more time.
common_mistakes.reason: The 'what' clause is treated as singular.

other_examples.sentence: Whatever you decide is fine with me.
other_examples.translation: Apa pun yang kamu putuskan baik-baik saja bagi saya.

explanation.en: 'Whatever you decide' is the subject.

questions.question: The sentence may contain 0, 1, or multiple errors. Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form. If no error, choose No Error.
questions.explanation: The verb 'admit' is followed by a gerund (V-ing), not an infinitive.

description.en: Certain verbs are strictly followed by a gerund, while others take an infinitive.
description.id: Kata kerja tertentu secara ketat diikuti oleh gerund, sementara yang lain mengambil infinitif.

wrong_correct.wrong: The CEO admitted to make a strategic error.
wrong_correct.correct: The CEO admitted making a strategic error.

explanation.en: 'Admit' is directly followed by a gerund.

en.introduction: Verb patterns must be memorized as they do not always follow logical rules.

rules.title: 1. Verbs + Gerund
rules.explanation: Verbs like admit, avoid, deny, suggest take a gerund.
rules.structure: Subject + verb + V-ing
notes: 'Admit to' can be used, but 'to' is a preposition, so it still takes a gerund.

common_mistakes.wrong: She denied to steal the money.
common_mistakes.correct: She denied stealing the money.

other_examples.sentence: I regret informing you that your application was rejected.
other_examples.translation: Saya menyesal memberi tahu Anda bahwa lamaran Anda ditolak.

explanation.en: 'Regret' + gerund refers to a past action.
explanation.id: 'Regret' + gerund merujuk pada tindakan masa lalu.

questions.question: The sentence may contain 0, 1, or multiple errors. Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form. If no error, choose No Error.
questions.explanation: The sentence is correct. 'Those' is used correctly as a substitute for 'the results' to avoid repetition.

description.en: Substitution uses words like 'one(s)', 'so', or 'those' to replace a noun phrase and avoid repetition.
description.id: Substitusi menggunakan kata seperti 'one(s)', 'so', atau 'those' untuk menggantikan frasa kata benda dan menghindari pengulangan.

en.introduction: Substitution creates cohesion and conciseness in comparative structures.

rules.title: 1. Demonstrative Substitution
rules.explanation: Use 'that' for singular and 'those' for plural nouns.
rules.structure: Noun phrase + than + those/that + of + noun
notes: 'Those' refers back to 'results'.

common_mistakes.wrong: The cars here are faster than the cars in Japan.
common_mistakes.correct: The cars here are faster than those in Japan.

other_examples.sentence: The climate of this region is milder than that of the north.
other_examples.translation: Iklim wilayah ini lebih sejuk daripada iklim di utara.

explanation.en: 'That' substitutes for 'the climate'.

questions.question: The sentence may contain 0, 1, or multiple errors. Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form. If no error, choose No Error.
questions.explanation: In formal American English, collective nouns like 'team' are treated as singular and require singular pronouns ('its').

description.en: Collective nouns can be singular or plural depending on whether the group acts as a single unit or as individuals.
description.id: Kata benda kolektif bisa tunggal atau jamak tergantung pada apakah kelompok bertindak sebagai satu unit atau sebagai individu.

wrong_correct.wrong: The team published their findings.
wrong_correct.correct: The team published its findings.

explanation.en: In formal contexts, 'team' is a single unit, requiring 'its'.
explanation.id: Dalam konteks formal, 'team' adalah satu unit, memerlukan 'its'.

en.introduction: Consistency in number (singular/plural) is crucial for formal writing.

rules.title: 1. Collective Noun Agreement
rules.explanation: Treat the collective noun as singular if it acts as one unit.
rules.structure: Collective noun + singular verb + singular pronoun
notes: Examples: team, committee, government, family.

common_mistakes.wrong: The committee has made their decision.
common_mistakes.correct: The committee has made its decision.

other_examples.sentence: The audience was captivated by its performance.
other_examples.translation: Penonton terpukau oleh penampilannya.

explanation.en: 'Audience' treated as a single entity.

questions.question: The sentence may contain 0, 1, or multiple errors. Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form. If no error, choose No Error.
questions.explanation: In formal contexts, 'conduct business' is the correct collocation, not 'do business'.

description.en: Collocations are words that naturally go together. Formal English requires specific verb-noun pairings.
description.id: Kolokasi adalah kata-kata yang secara alami saling menyertai. Bahasa Inggris formal memerlukan pasangan kata kerja-kata benda tertentu.

wrong_correct.wrong: Companies do business globally.
wrong_correct.correct: Companies conduct business globally.

explanation.en: 'Conduct' is the formal verb collocated with 'business'.
explanation.id: 'Conduct' adalah kata kerja formal yang berkolokasi dengan 'business'.

en.introduction: Using precise collocations elevates the formality and accuracy of writing.

rules.title: 1. Formal Verb-Noun Collocations
rules.explanation: Replace informal verbs with formal equivalents.
rules.structure: conduct business, make a decision, pose a threat
notes: Avoid 'do', 'make', 'get' in formal academic writing where specific verbs exist.

common_mistakes.wrong: We need to do a thorough investigation.
common_mistakes.correct: We need to conduct a thorough investigation.
common_mistakes.reason: 'Conduct' is the appropriate formal verb for 'investigation'.

other_examples.sentence: The government will implement new policies.
other_examples.translation: Pemerintah akan menerapkan kebijakan baru.

explanation.en: 'Implement' collocates with 'policies'.

questions.question: The sentence may contain 0, 1, or multiple errors. Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form. If no error, choose No Error.
questions.explanation: With reporting verbs in the passive, the correct structure is 'Subject + is believed + to infinitive', not 'is believed that it + verb'.

description.en: Impersonal passive structures are used to report beliefs, claims, or knowledge formally.
description.id: Struktur pasif impersonal digunakan untuk melaporkan kepercayaan, klaim, atau pengetahuan secara formal.

wrong_correct.wrong: The artifact is believed that it dates back.
wrong_correct.correct: The artifact is believed to date back.

explanation.en: Use 'to + infinitive' after passive reporting verbs.
explanation.id: Gunakan 'to + infinitive' setelah kata kerja pelaporan pasif.

en.introduction: This structure is common in journalism and academic writing.

rules.title: 1. Personal Passive Structure
rules.explanation: The subject of the active clause becomes the subject of the passive clause.
rules.structure: Subject + is/are + believed/said/thought + to + V1
notes: For past events, use 'to have + V3'.

common_mistakes.wrong: He is said that he is rich.
common_mistakes.correct: He is said to be rich.
common_mistakes.reason: The 'that' clause is incorrect in this personal passive structure.

other_examples.sentence: The suspect is thought to have fled the country.
other_examples.translation: Tersangka diduga telah melarikan diri ke luar negeri.

explanation.en: 'To have fled' indicates a past action.
explanation.id: 'To have fled' menunjukkan tindakan masa lalu.

questions.question: The sentence may contain 0, 1, or multiple errors. Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form. If no error, choose No Error.
questions.explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct. 'Despite the fact that' is properly followed by a full clause.

description.en: 'Despite the fact that' is a formal conjunction followed by a subject and verb.
description.id: 'Despite the fact that' adalah konjungsi formal yang diikuti oleh subjek dan kata kerja.

en.introduction: Both 'despite' and 'despite the fact that' are correct, but their grammatical requirements differ.

rules.title: 1. Despite vs. Despite the fact that
rules.explanation: 'Despite' + noun phrase; 'Despite the fact that' + clause.
rules.structure: Despite + noun phrase OR Despite the fact that + subject + verb
notes: Never use 'despite of'.

common_mistakes.wrong: Despite of the rain, we went out.
common_mistakes.correct: Despite the rain, we went out.

other_examples.sentence: In spite of the heavy traffic, we arrived on time.
other_examples.translation: Meskipun lalu lintas padat, kami tiba tepat waktu.

explanation.en: 'In spite of' + noun phrase.

questions.question: The sentence may contain 0, 1, or multiple errors. Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form. If no error, choose No Error.
questions.explanation: The sentence is correct. 'Subsequently', 'validated', and 'rigorous' are used correctly in formal academic context.

description.en: Academic writing requires precise vocabulary and correct adverb placement.
description.id: Penulisan akademis memerlukan kosakata yang tepat dan penempatan kata keterangan yang benar.

en.introduction: Words like 'subsequently', 'validated', and 'rigorous' are hallmarks of C1/C2 academic English.

rules.title: 1. Formal Adverb Placement
rules.explanation: Adverbs of time/sequence often appear before the main verb.
rules.structure: Subject + auxiliary + adverb + past participle
notes: 'Subsequently' means 'after that' or 'later'.

common_mistakes.wrong: The hypothesis was validated rigorous.
common_mistakes.correct: The hypothesis was validated by rigorous experiments.
common_mistakes.reason: Adjective 'rigorous' must modify a noun, not a verb.

other_examples.sentence: The theory was initially proposed in the 19th century.
other_examples.translation: Teori tersebut awalnya diusulkan pada abad ke-19.

explanation.en: 'Initially' correctly modifies 'proposed'.

questions.question: The sentence may contain 0, 1, or multiple errors. Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form. If no error, choose No Error.
questions.explanation: The sentence is correct. 'Only after' at the beginning of a sentence triggers inversion in the main clause.

description.en: When 'only' + a time expression begins a sentence, the main clause requires inversion.
description.id: Ketika 'only' + ekspresi waktu mengawali kalimat, klausa utama memerlukan inversi.

en.introduction: This structure emphasizes the condition that must be met before the main action occurs.

rules.title: 1. Only + Time Expression
rules.explanation: The subordinate clause remains normal; the main clause is inverted.
rules.structure: Only after + clause, auxiliary + subject + main verb
notes: The inversion happens in the main clause, not the 'only' clause.

common_mistakes.wrong: Only after he left, I realized the truth.
common_mistakes.correct: Only after he left did I realize the truth.

other_examples.sentence: Only when the rain stopped could we continue the journey.
other_examples.translation: Hanya ketika hujan berhenti kami bisa melanjutkan perjalanan.

explanation.en: Inversion 'could we' in the main clause.

questions.question: The sentence may contain 0, 1, or multiple errors. Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form. If no error, choose No Error.
questions.explanation: 1. 'A series' is singular, so it requires 'is scheduled'. 2. 'On' is not used before 'next Monday'.

description.en: Advanced sentences may contain multiple distinct errors, such as subject-verb agreement and preposition misuse.
description.id: Kalimat lanjutan mungkin mengandung beberapa kesalahan berbeda.

wrong_correct.wrong: A series of lectures are scheduled on next Monday.
wrong_correct.correct: A series of lectures is scheduled next Monday.

explanation.en: 'Series' is singular; 'next Monday' does not take 'on'.

en.introduction: Careful proofreading is required to catch multiple error types in a single sentence.

rules.title: 1. Collective/Quantifier Agreement
rules.explanation: 'A series', 'each' are singular.
rules.structure: A series of + plural noun + singular verb
notes: Focus on the head noun, not the noun in the prepositional phrase.

common_mistakes.wrong: We will meet on next week.
common_mistakes.correct: We will meet next week.
common_mistakes.reason: Do not use prepositions of time before 'next', 'last', or 'this'.

other_examples.sentence: A pair of shoes was left in the hallway.
other_examples.translation: Sepasang sepatu tertinggal di lorong.

explanation.en: 'A pair' is singular.

questions.question: The sentence may contain 0, 1, or multiple errors. Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form. If no error, choose No Error.
questions.explanation: Parallelism requires all items after 'responsible for' to be gerunds: 'training', 'evaluating', and 'assigning'.

description.en: Items in a list following a preposition must all be in the gerund form.
description.id: Item dalam daftar yang mengikuti preposisi harus semuanya dalam bentuk gerund.

wrong_correct.wrong: Responsible for training, to evaluate, and to assign.
wrong_correct.correct: Responsible for training, evaluating, and assigning.

explanation.en: All items must be gerunds to maintain parallel structure.
explanation.id: Semua item harus berupa gerund untuk mempertahankan struktur paralel.

en.introduction: Parallelism ensures that the reader can easily follow the list of responsibilities.

rules.title: 1. Gerund Lists
rules.explanation: After a preposition, all coordinated verbs must be gerunds.
rules.structure: for + V-ing, V-ing, and V-ing
notes: Do not mix infinitives and gerunds in the same list.

common_mistakes.wrong: She is interested in learning, to teach, and researching.
common_mistakes.correct: She is interested in learning, teaching, and researching.

other_examples.sentence: He is known for writing, editing, and publishing his own books.
other_examples.translation: Dia dikenal karena menulis, mengedit, dan menerbitkan bukunya sendiri.

explanation.en: All gerunds follow 'for'.

questions.question: The sentence may contain 0, 1, or multiple errors. Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form. If no error, choose No Error.
questions.explanation: 'Were I to accept' is a formal second conditional. The main clause must use 'would + base verb', not 'will'.

description.en: 'Were + subject + to + verb' is a formal alternative to 'If + subject + past simple' in second conditionals.
description.id: 'Were + subjek + to + kata kerja' adalah alternatif formal untuk 'If + subjek + past simple'.

wrong_correct.wrong: Were I to accept the position, I will relocate.
wrong_correct.correct: Were I to accept the position, I would relocate.

explanation.en: Second conditional requires 'would' in the main clause, not 'will'.
explanation.id: Conditional kedua memerlukan 'would' di klausa utama, bukan 'will'.

en.introduction: This structure is highly formal and common in professional or academic contexts.

rules.title: 1. Inverted Second Conditional
rules.explanation: Omits 'if' and inverts 'were' and the subject.
rules.structure: Were + subject + to + V1, subject + would + V1
notes: Only used with 'were', not 'was'.

common_mistakes.wrong: Were he to ask, I will help him.
common_mistakes.correct: Were he to ask, I would help him.

other_examples.sentence: Should you need any assistance, please contact us.
other_examples.translation: Jika Anda memerlukan bantuan, silakan hubungi kami.

explanation.en: 'Should you need' is a formal first conditional inversion.
explanation.id: 'Should you need' adalah inversi conditional pertama yang formal.

questions.question: The sentence may contain 0, 1, or multiple errors. Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form. If no error, choose No Error.
questions.explanation: The subject 'proposals' is plural, so the verb must be 'were'. 'Presented at the conference' is a correctly reduced relative clause.

description.en: Relative clauses can be reduced to participle phrases when the relative pronoun is the subject.
description.id: Klausa relatif dapat direduksi menjadi frasa partisip ketika kata ganti relatif adalah subjek.

wrong_correct.wrong: The proposals presented at the conference was innovative.
wrong_correct.correct: The proposals presented at the conference were innovative.

explanation.en: The head noun 'proposals' is plural, requiring a plural verb.
explanation.id: Kata benda utama 'proposals' adalah jamak, memerlukan kata kerja jamak.

en.introduction: Reduction makes sentences more concise without losing meaning.

rules.title: 1. Passive Reduction
rules.explanation: Remove the relative pronoun and 'be' verb.
rules.structure: Noun + past participle phrase
notes: 'The proposals (which were) presented...'

common_mistakes.wrong: The students who studying hard passed the exam.
common_mistakes.correct: The students studying hard passed the exam.
common_mistakes.reason: In reduced relative clauses, do not keep the relative pronoun if you remove the 'be' verb.

other_examples.sentence: The data collected over ten years shows a clear trend.
other_examples.translation: Data yang dikumpulkan selama sepuluh tahun menunjukkan tren yang jelas.

explanation.en: 'Collected over ten years' modifies 'data'.

questions.question: The sentence may contain 0, 1, or multiple errors. Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form. If no error, choose No Error.
questions.explanation: Double comparatives use 'the + comparative', not 'the more + comparative'. 'Higher' is already comparative.

description.en: Double comparatives express that two things change together.
description.id: Komparatif ganda mengekspresikan bahwa dua hal berubah bersama.

wrong_correct.wrong: The more complex it is, the more higher the cost.
wrong_correct.correct: The more complex it is, the higher the cost.

explanation.en: Use 'the + comparative', not 'the more + comparative'.

en.introduction: This structure is used to show proportional correlation.

rules.title: 1. The + Comparative, The + Comparative
rules.explanation: Both clauses must start with 'the' followed by a comparative form.
rules.structure: The + comparative + subject + verb, the + comparative + subject + verb
notes: Do not use 'more' with adjectives that already have '-er'.

common_mistakes.wrong: The more you practice, the more better you get.
common_mistakes.correct: The more you practice, the better you get.

other_examples.sentence: The sooner we start, the earlier we will finish.
other_examples.translation: Semakin cepat kita mulai, semakin awal kita akan selesai.

explanation.en: Correct double comparative structure.

questions.question: The sentence may contain 0, 1, or multiple errors. Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form. If no error, choose No Error.
questions.explanation: The sentence is correct. It properly uses a concessive clause and the present perfect tense to connect past action to present relevance.

description.en: Complex sentences combine an independent clause with one or more dependent clauses.
description.id: Kalimat kompleks menggabungkan klausa independen dengan satu atau lebih klausa dependen.

en.introduction: Mastering complex sentences is key to C1/C2 writing proficiency.

rules.title: 1. Concessive + Main Clause
rules.explanation: A contrast is established, followed by the main point.
rules.structure: Although + clause, main clause
notes: Do not use 'but' in the main clause if 'Although' is used.

common_mistakes.wrong: Although it was raining, but we went out.
common_mistakes.correct: Although it was raining, we went out.
common_mistakes.reason: 'Although' and 'but' cannot be used in the same sentence.

other_examples.sentence: Even though the task was difficult, she completed it successfully.
other_examples.translation: Meskipun tugasnya sulit, dia menyelesaikannya dengan sukses.

explanation.en: Correct use of 'Even though' without 'but'.

questions.question: The sentence may contain 0, 1, or multiple errors. Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form. If no error, choose No Error.
questions.explanation: The causative 'have' is followed by an object and the base form of the verb (have someone do something), not the infinitive ('to review').

description.en: The causative 'have' indicates that the subject arranged for someone else to perform an action.
description.id: Kausatif 'have' menunjukkan bahwa subjek mengatur agar orang lain melakukan suatu tindakan.

wrong_correct.wrong: I had the mechanic to fix my car.
wrong_correct.correct: I had the mechanic fix my car.

explanation.en: Causative 'have' takes the base verb, not the infinitive.
explanation.id: Kausatif 'have' mengambil kata kerja dasar, bukan infinitif.

en.introduction: This structure is essential for describing delegated actions formally.

rules.title: 1. Active Causative
rules.explanation: Subject + have + person + base verb + object.
rules.structure: Subject + had + someone + V1 + object
notes: Alternatively, 'get + someone + to + V1' can be used.

common_mistakes.wrong: She had her assistant to prepare the report.
common_mistakes.correct: She had her assistant prepare the report.
common_mistakes.reason: 'Have' is followed by the base verb, not 'to + verb'.

other_examples.sentence: We will have the IT department install the new software.
other_examples.translation: Kami akan meminta departemen TI menginstal perangkat lunak baru.

explanation.en: 'Have' + object + base verb.
